instruction: Find the origin and meaning of the name Emma on BabyCenter.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully navigated from babycenter.com/child to Baby Names section, searched for 'Carl', found the details page at babycenter.com/baby-names/details/carl-853, and scrolled to the similar names section. Handled privacy dialog and signup popup along the way.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can handle privacy dialogs and popups, navigate babycenter.com navigation menu, use the baby name search feature, scroll through page content to find specific sections
metadata.task_rationale: Same pattern as original (navigate to a baby name details page) but with a different name. Tests the model's ability to search for and navigate to a different name's details page.
metadata.explanation: Task requires navigating from babycenter.com/child to the baby names section, searching for 'Emma', and reaching the Emma details page. Evaluator checks that the active URL matches the babycenter baby name details page for Emma using regex pattern matching.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly extracts the active Chrome tab URL, which is the right state to verify navigation to the Emma details page.
Metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) uses re.search for partial matching, which correctly handles BabyCenter URLs that may include a numeric suffix (e.g., /emma-12345).
Expected pattern 'babycenter\.com/baby-names/details/emma' is semantically correct for the task of finding Emma's name details on BabyCenter.
Metric parameter handling is correct: rules dict is accessed directly as expected when type='rule'.

Minor limitation: URL-only verification is a proxy for 'finding origin and meaning' — it confirms navigation to the correct page but not that information was actually read. This is standard OSWorld practice and acceptable.
